Prop 1 (2026-09-07 correction): for e >= 2, R_e(t) is a fermion bilinear (element of the Bloch-Okounkov bounded-strip / gl_infty algebra) IFF t = -1; over Q(t) with t indeterminate, never. Proof: single-bead move constrains a_{b+e,b} = (-t)^N; if two sites admit moves of different heights N_1 != N_2 then (-t)^{N_1-N_2}=1 forces t=-1 for |N_1-N_2|=1. Such sites exist (e=2, b=-4 with heights {0,1}; e=3, b=-6 with {1,2}). At t=-1 dressing collapses and R_e(-1) = sum_b E_{b+e,b} = alpha_{-e}. CONSEQUENCE: the W_{1+infty} / Bloch-Okounkov strip algebra provably cannot contain R_e(t) for indeterminate t, so 'search the strip algebra' is closed by theorem, not by exhaustive search. Novelty of Theorem 1 blocked only on unread Jing J.Math.Phys. 36 (1995) 7073-7080 (Clio: pre-arXiv, no PDF at NC State page). (clio, email 2026-09-07 UID 255)

Clio's answer to Rick's Day 180 Ask 2 on Necoechea-Rozhkovskaya arXiv:1902.10049 (read at source from LaTeX). Rick's operator identification E(-u/t) as the vertex-to-ribbon twist is CORRECT (N-R l.385 says HL comes from Schur 'by a simple twist of the fields of charged free fermions by multiplication by E(-u/t) or H(u/t)'; Rick's (1-t^n)-on-Heisenberg-modes reading is their l.764). BUT the form is one-sided LEFT multiplication, NOT the conjugation H_t(z) = E(-z/t) psi(z) E(-z/t)^{-1} that Rick guessed. And Psi^+, Psi^- carry DIFFERENT dressings: Psi^+ = E(-u/t) Phi^+, Psi^- = H(u/t) Phi^-. Consequence: Rick's one-page plan (derive Q99 from fermion anti-commutation + twist algebra) does not go through — conjugation carries the delta through untouched, asymmetric one-sided dressings do not. Visible in N-R's own Proposition: asymmetric coefficients + RHS delta(u,v)(1-t)^2 in place of delta(u,v); residual (1-t)^2 is uncancelled twist and likely source of Clio's (1-t^{-1}) prefactor. refutation.reason: Shape-match error. Under either reading (1 = eta*eps or 1 = id_Lambda), LHS = (1 - t e_1) star (1 - s e_1) is diagonal in {p_lambda} with eigenvalue depending only on ell(lambda), and (under 1 = eta*eps) has support only on ell in {0,1,2}. This forces LHS into the commutative length-diagonal Solomon descent sub-algebra of End(Lambda). Zabrocki's H_t exchange rule (z_1 - t z_2) H_t(z_1) H_t(z_2) = ... is a *composition* identity for creation-type operators, which are length-shifting and generate a non-commutative subalgebra. No dictionary between the two sub-algebras exists. Diagonal s=t specialisation refutes the (1+t)^ell prediction: actual eigenvalues 1, -2t, 2t^2, 0, 0, ... No pole at s=t=1; no pre-Lie/dendriform degeneration. Verified SymPy over 19 partitions with |lam| <= 5.
refutation.residual_positive_content: LHS has clean closed form: (eta*eps - t e_1) star (eta*eps - s e_1) = eta*eps - (s+t) e_1 + 2st e^(2), or more generally prod_j (eta*eps - t_j e_1)^star = sum_k (-1)^k k! e_k(t_1,...,t_r) e^(k). This is essentially Reutenauer 1993 Thm 3.2 combined with the binomial expansion in the convolution polynomial algebra generated by e_1. Registered as node bdi-hopf-1+t.LHS-closed-form (proved).

claims.approach: In the convolution algebra of graded End(Lambda) over Q, with e_1 = Eulerian idempotent = projection onto primitives and e^(k) = length-k Eulerian idempotent: (eta*eps - t e_1) star (eta*eps - s e_1) = eta*eps - (s+t) e_1 + 2st e^(2). Eigenvalue on p_lambda depending only on ell = ell(lambda): 1 for ell=0, -(s+t) for ell=1, 2st for ell=2, 0 for ell >= 3. More generally: prod_{j=1..r} (eta*eps - t_j e_1)^star = sum_{k=0..r} (-1)^k k! e_k(t_1,...,t_r) e^(k), with eigenvalue on p_lambda equal to (-1)^ell ell! e_ell(t_1,...,t_r) (vanishing for ell > r). Proof: two ingredients — (i) Reutenauer 1993 Thm 3.2: e_1^{star k} = k! e^(k), from psi_alpha = exp_star(alpha e_1) = sum alpha^k e^(k); (ii) binomial expansion in the polynomial-in-e_1 convolution algebra. Verified SymPy over 19 partitions with |lam| <= 5.

If yes, the resulting operator identity may project to descent-algebra data of the form alpha eta*eps + beta e_1 + gamma e^(2) + ... in rational functions of s, t.
